title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Innate Immunity and Infection
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 9, Extension Topic A · 9 questions · 67 marks · 30 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question. If a question cannot be traced to a paper, it is not in here.

Nine questions, 67 marks, 30 parts. The set is sized for coverage, not for the clock. Cluster 1 owns the innate half of one learning outcome, LO (a), which is the smallest concept in Book 9 at the papers. Nine questions is what complete coverage of that half costs, and it is deliberately not padded out to 90 marks.

Suggest is the command word to prepare for. Suggest is 23.8% of every structured part in this Book, nearly double Book 3's share, so about a quarter of what you will be asked has no recall answer available at all. Seven parts below are Suggest parts on pathogens, tissues and methods the notes never mention: Salmonella, Helicobacter, cockroach allergen, buffalo lymphocytes, wound fluid, an unfamiliar assay and asymptomatic influenza carriers. Learn the causal chain, not the list.

Question 4 is the full-cycle question. It runs one continuous chain: a pathogen crosses a barrier, the innate system recognises it, phagocytes are recruited, inflammation follows, cytokines reach the hypothalamus, symptoms appear, and then the last part asks what happens when the same chain is too small to produce any symptom at all. Answer (a) to (d) as one story.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. Q2(a) is VJC Prelim 2025 Paper 1 Question 28 word for word and Q3(a) is CJC Prelim 2023 Paper 1 Question 27 word for word. The paper awards one mark for the letter. Say why each of the other three options is wrong before you reveal.

Two real figures, and honesty about the rest. Q2 carries VJC Prelim 2025 Paper 2 Fig. 4.2 and Q7 carries VJC Prelim 2025 Paper 2 Fig. 10.1, both lifted from the paper itself. Every other figure comes from a paper whose PDF is not in the papers, so the question carries that paper's own printed description rather than a redrawing, and says so on the page.

Cumulative over Books 1 to 8. Q1(c) needs the peptidoglycan wall from Book 4. Q2(c) needs lysosome structure from Book 1 and Q2(e) needs membrane fluidity from Book 1. Q3(b) needs transcription factors from Book 2 and cancer from Book 3. Q8(b) needs a full signal transduction pathway from Book 3 written link by link. Q9(a) needs ligand, receptor and phosphorylation cascade from Book 3. A Book 1 to 4 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 1 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Read which line of defence the stem asks about before you write, because a marker's note in this file states that on a first-line question adaptive immune responses were not accepted. Name the compartment: phagosome, then phagolysosome after lysosome fusion. Write interferon, not cytokine, whenever the answer is antiviral resistance. Quote figures off any diagram you are told to refer to, because a school examiner's note says to quote data even if the question did not explicitly direct you to do so.

Four errors in your own Book 9 notes are targeted here. Q3(a) option C punishes printed page 19, which calls dendritic cells differentiated macrophages. Q3(b) carries the correction to printed page 20, which inverts how a natural killer cell reads MHC. Q6(a) carries the correction to the specificity contradiction on printed pages 15 and 16. Q2(c) carries the correction to printed page 24, which puts antibodies inside a second-line answer.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not only duplicated labels. Q1 the first line at a mucosal surface, and two pathogens that defeat it · Q2 phagocytosis by compartment, organelle and membrane · Q3 the innate cells and proteins that act on host cells rather than on microbes · Q4 the whole innate cycle from breach to symptom · Q5 complement, and innate proteins in an unfamiliar fluid · Q6 the two systems compared, and what antibody hands back to the innate system · Q7 antigen, presentation and the bridge into the third line · Q8 innate immunity read off a signal transduction pathway · Q9 cell signalling as the mechanism of coordination.

The one shared marking point in the set is that phagocytosis occurs, which Q2 needs alongside the compartment names and Q4(a) needs alongside PRR recognition and phagocyte recruitment. The two schemes credit different halves of the outcome, so the answers do not collapse into each other; if you gave Q2's phagosome answer in Q4(a) you answered the wrong half. Nothing else in the set repeats.

Nothing from Clusters 2 or 3, and nothing from Book 4's viral cycles. Clonal selection, clonal expansion, primary against secondary responses, MHC class I against class II in full, antibody diversity, the four types of immunity, vaccination, R0 and the epidemiology terms are all later. No question here sets a viral replication cycle, which belongs to Core Idea 2 LO 2(e) in Book 4.
